original: Not defined. Figma has Desktop, Tablet and Mobile modes with no pixel widths.
reason: These are the widths the design.dga.gov.sa CSS uses and also Tailwind's defaults. Figma's tablet frame is 704 + 2×32 = 768px wide, which matches md.

original: tokens.css (extraction guess): Desktop default, Tablet at max-width 1024px, Mobile at max-width 640px
ours: Mobile-first: Mobile is the base, Tablet from 768px (md), Desktop from 1024px (lg)
reason: Mobile-first matches Tailwind's min-width breakpoints, and 768px is where Figma's tablet grid starts.

original: Mobile mode: text-md 12px, text-sm 10px, text-xs 8px; Tablet: text-md 14px
ours: Body text sizes stay at their desktop values on every viewport. Display sizes still follow the Figma modes.
reason: 8–12px body text is hard to read on phones, iOS zooms into inputs under 16px, and the mobile mode made text-lg (14px) smaller than text-md.

ours: [data-theme="dark"] and .dark (both work, also on any subtree)
reason: shadcn and next-themes use the .dark class. All semantic tokens are re-declared in the dark scope so nested dark sections resolve correctly.

original: shadcn derives radius-sm…4xl from --radius with calc()
ours: Fixed DGA radii: none 0, xs 2, sm 4, md 8, lg 16, xl 24, full 9999px; --radius = radius-sm (4px)
reason: DGA defines exact radii. Buttons and inputs use radius-sm (4px).

ours: Tailwind's --spacing: 0.25rem, so p-4 = 16px and p-80 = 320px, matching DGA one-to-one
reason: rem keeps spacing in step with the user's root font size. The raw --spacing-* variables keep their px values.

ours: Audited per component as each one lands (Phase 2+)
reason: Phase 1 audits foundation tokens only: text, links and icons on surfaces, and on-colour text on fills.

original: Flips to white in dark mode
reason: It is an inverse surface (white in dark mode), so text on it must use the inverse colour, not text-oncolor-primary. Primary-neutral buttons use button-background-black-*, which stays dark.

ours: Use only on deep fills: nav header, pressed/selected primary, black. On mid-tone fills use --text-oncolor-primary.
reason: White itself is only 4.57–4.83:1 on the 600-level fills, so no lower opacity can pass there. On deep fills 80% and 70% white pass AA.
